title: GreenMix: Energy-Efficient Serverless Computing via Randomized Sketching on Asymmetric Multi-Cores
problem: Serverless computing on asymmetric multi-core processors (big.LITTLE, Alder Lake) presents optimization challenges for energy efficiency and keep-alive costs while maintaining QoS targets.
motivation: Asymmetric multi-cores offer superior energy-performance trade-offs through heterogeneous core types. Existing serverless schedulers ignore these benefits, missing opportunities for energy reduction. Keep-alive costs in serverless add significant overhead.
method: GreenMix uses randomized sketching algorithm tailored for serverless execution to optimally assign functions to core types. Targets energy minimization and keep-alive cost reduction while respecting QoS constraints. Evaluated on ARM big.LITTLE and Intel Alder Lake systems.
key_novelty: First serverless scheduler leveraging asymmetric multi-cores for combined energy and keep-alive cost optimization, using randomized sketching approximation.
contributions: First work integrating asymmetric multi-core awareness into serverless scheduling
Randomized sketching algorithm for function-to-core assignment
Joint optimization of energy efficiency and keep-alive costs
Evaluation on ARM big.LITTLE and Intel Alder Lake processors
10% of optimal energy efficiency and keep-alive cost reduction
limitations: Sketching approximation (10% gap to optimal) may limit gains on smaller systems. Scalability to very large serverless clusters not evaluated. Real production workload evaluation missing. Keep-alive cost model assumptions not detailed.
primary_theme: Energy-efficient serverless computing on heterogeneous hardware
